chapter: MJQ, Pettiford and the move to Paris
title: Pushing Cannonball to sign with Columbia
summary: Cannonball hesitated over a $10,000 Columbia offer because he did not want to leave Clarke; Clarke insisted he sign, and he went on to success.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: So one day, this was about two or three weeks later, Cannonball comes over the hotel and he says, "Listen, Klook, I don't know how to tell you this." I said,
"Look, Cannon, you can tell me anything." He said, "This guy at Columbia, Quincy was over there." Bob -- the A&R man. You know.

Bob Field. He says, "They've offered me 10 grand," he says, "But man, I can't leave you." I said, "Look, if I had a stick I would beat you all the way to Bob Thiele's Fields office and make you sign." So that was -- so he says, "Really, Klook Kluke?" I said, "Look," I said, "As long as I've been in New York, I've never had anyone offer me $10,000.00." I said, "If you don't take that $10,000.00, I'll kill you and ship you back to Florida." And he took the -- from then on -- well, we went to -- with his -- he played with us with the Modern Jazz Quartet. We played the Blue Note in Philly, and the cat would say, "Well, who you want on the bill?" I'd say, "Well, how about Monk, Cannonball," you know, I'd be screaming for Cannonball. So then he made this thing, this Ernie Wilkins arrangement on the album with Sarah Vaughan, and that did it. He went on from there.
Well, you never know, do you?
And just as Cannonball had gotten big, you know, at the time --
